events_rail.explain: Cash rises from ¥550k to ¥805k. Your minimum is ¥300k, so ¥505k of room remains.

events_rail.label: payroll is paid
events_rail.explain: Cash falls from ¥805k to ¥465k. Your minimum is ¥300k, so ¥165k of room remains. Without the financing plan, payroll would have taken cash to ¥60k, below your minimum.

events_rail.label: a supplier payment goes out
events_rail.explain: Cash falls from ¥465k to ¥345k. Your minimum is ¥300k, so ¥45k of room remains. Without the financing plan, the supplier payment would have taken cash to −¥60k, below your minimum.

events_rail.label: a loan repayment goes out
events_rail.note: cash at its lowest, ¥300k, at your minimum
events_rail.explain: This is the lowest point on your cash line: ¥300k, ¥0 above your minimum. Debt service of ¥45k takes cash from ¥345k to ¥300k. Without the financing plan, the lowest point would have been −¥105k in 30 days.

stress.assumption_text: If Foshan Home Retail Co. paid every invoice 30 days late (a test, not a forecast). The ¥255,000 financing on the ¥420,000.00 invoice to Foshan Home Retail Co. (due in 32 days) runs 30 days longer: about ¥2,270 more in charges, as its agreement sets them.
